subtype: Approach: tries the same action in different ways until something works [Action]
passage: Nursery note. Baljeet, two, sat on the mat with the shape box and pushed the round block at the square hole. It did not go. Baljeet turned it over and pushed again, then pressed harder with both hands and grunted. Then Baljeet tried the round hole, and the block dropped in with a clunk. Baljeet clapped and looked up at me. I only smiled. Preeti, sitting beside, tried the same block in the square hole and laughed.

qa.q: What sound did the block make?
qa.a: The block dropped in with a clunk.

qa.q: How did Baljeet seem to feel when the block dropped in?
qa.a: Baljeet seemed pleased and proud, clapping and looking up at the adult.

qa.q: What could the caregiver do next time Baljeet is stuck?
qa.a: The caregiver could let Baljeet keep trying and give a small hint only if Baljeet gets upset.

qa.q: How might Preeti have seen what Baljeet did?
qa.a: Preeti was probably curious, since Preeti tried the same block in the square hole and laughed.

grounding: Shows a toddler trying a round block in a square hole by turning it and pressing harder, then moving to the round hole where it drops in.
